title: Legal and ethical ground: interoperability, MIT headers, and what was never taken apart
summary: CUDA++ uses 67 MIT headers from NVIDIA's open kernel module, unchanged; Mesa NVK/NAK facts are cited, not copied; Drake ran nvcc and cuobjdump only on his own probe kernels, took apart no NVIDIA program, and ships no firmware. The audit says it is not a legal opinion. Re-checking the pinned tree finds three things to know: two cubins that are CUDA++'s own exports, an nvdisasm-made golden file, and AGPL-3.0-only tags on native .om files under an Apache LICENSE.
goal: Know exactly what CUDA++ used from NVIDIA and under which terms, and check those statements against the tree.
key_steps: Count the vendored headers and their licence lines.
Read NVIDIA COPYING for the scope of the GPL option.
Search the tree for binaries and NVIDIA tool listings.
Read what HOW_I_DID_IT.md says was and was not done.
Check the SPDX line of any file before reusing it.

common_mistake: Overclaiming either way: NVIDIA tools were used offline on Drake's own probes (not never), and CUDApp contains NVIDIA's MIT headers (not NVIDIA code beyond them). Cite the file and leave legal conclusions to lawyers.
